S1 — MATERIAL (P2), packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolResolveCheck.ts:223. The additional label-token guard rejects legitimate situational modifiers, exceeding the source-based guard specified in dispatch decision 3 and violating its requirement to add other caller modifiers such as cover. Concrete reproduced scenario: a stored-sheet character with DEX modifier +3, kind=saving_throw, ability=dexterity, vs=15, modifiers=[{label:"Dexterity saving throw bonus from half cover",value:2,source:"cover:half"}] returns invalid_args and tells the caller to remove the modifier. The identical call with label="half cover" succeeds (natural 10 + DEX 3 + cover 2 = 15). This bonus is independently required by SRD Cover (+2 to Dexterity saving throws); it does not duplicate the sheet-derived ability modifier. The defect class extends to descriptive labels for other legitimate save/check bonuses that mention the governing ability. Suggested fix: retain the mandated source-based guard, but remove or narrow the additional any-token label guard so descriptive situational labels are accepted; align the tool-description refusal guidance. Permanent evidence: generalized invariant in the existing derivation tests that admissibility and arithmetic of an allowed situational bonus do not change when only its descriptive label mentions the governing ability; keep separate baseline-ability/proficiency refusal evidence. This is proportionate to preventing refusal or omission of actual rules bonuses. Owner: PR implementer; repair before merge.

S2 — MATERIAL (P2), packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts:208. The system prompt applies "for a character with a sheet pass skill or ability" to every ability check, saving throw, AND attack, while forbidding that character from declaring ability/proficiency. Attack derivation is explicitly excluded by dispatch decision 4 and refused by deriveFromSheet. Concrete reproduced scenario: a sheet-backed Kira attacking with Dexterity follows the prompt using {kind:"attack",actor:"Kira",ability:"dexterity",vs:15,reason:"attack"} and receives invalid_args ("skill/ability derivation is not supported for attack rolls; declare modifiers instead"). The legacy declared-modifier/proficiency attack succeeds. Thus a prompt-conforming caller cannot resolve an ordinary character attack without contradicting the system instruction. This applies across weapon/spell attacks and governing abilities; monsters' declared path remains unaffected. Suggested fix: limit sheet-derived prompt guidance to ability checks and saving throws, and explicitly keep attacks on declared modifiers/proficiency regardless of sheet availability. Permanent evidence: generalized prompt/operation-scope regression in existing protocol/resolution tests distinguishing checks/saves from attacks, rather than a live-model test. Owner: PR implementer; repair before merge.

Verification: seven targeted test files passed, 102 tests total (resolveCheckSheetDerivation, skillBonuses, resolutionTools, resolution, playerVisibleRollLedger, protocol, turnTraceProjection). No worktree-local node_modules exists; ran the existing eshyra-r8en.1 Vitest installation against this worktree's exact source, with config/cache/temp storage outside the repository. Both findings were directly reproduced through ToolRegistry schema admission. git diff --check passed; repository status stayed clean; head remained the assigned SHA. No repository edits, verification formatter, commits, pushes, GitHub comments, or merge performed. No additional non-material findings published.
VERDICT: MATERIAL FINDINGS (2)
